t: #3827 Count Monobit Integers — Repunits Plus Zero
o: A monobit integer has all-equal binary digits: 0, and the repunits 1, 11, 111, ... in binary (values 1, 3, 7, 15, ...). Since n <= 1000, there are at most ~10 such repunits, so counting them directly is trivial. For n=4 the qualifying values are 0, 1, 3 giving answer 3.
k: The only monobit values are 0 and 2^j - 1 (binary repunits).
Just count repunits <= n and add 1 for zero.

a.i: Generate v = 1, 11, 111, ... (in decimal representation of binary repunits, i.e., v = v*10 + 1 interpreted as the binary value 2^j - 1 via repeated v = 2v+1... simplest is v = v*2 + 1) and count how many are <= n.
s: While v <= n, increment ans and set v = v*2 + 1.
a.t: O(log n) — one iteration per bit length.

a.i: For each x in [0, n], verify all bits of x are equal by comparing every bit to the lowest bit. Perfectly fine for n <= 1000.
s: For each x from 0 to n, let b = x & 1.
Shift x right; if any bit differs from b, reject.
a.t: O(n log n) — each number checked bit by bit.

w: The repunit formula is the interview-ready answer; the brute force is a sanity check. Edge cases: n = 0 returns 1 (just zero). Watch for overflow if generating repunits carelessly in fixed-width languages — use 64-bit or stop as soon as v exceeds n.
